clue.text: People plunge down these hills

parts.note: people in general can be called men
a plunge into water is a dip

explanation.surface: Holidaymakers go hurtling down a range of steep slopes.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mendips are a range of limestone hills in Somerset, south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Proper name of a range of Somerset hills, here pointed at by 'these'.

clue.text: The foreign cheese lacks a bit of moisture, which is to do with the weather

parts.note: el is Spanish for 'the', a foreign definite article

indicators.note: lacks says a letter is missing from the cheese named beside it

parts.note: Emmental is a Swiss cheese with holes

indicators.note: a bit of picks just the opening letter of the word moisture

explanation.surface: A complaint that some imported cheese has dried out, oddly tied to the climate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacks' takes away the first letter of 'moisture' from the cheese, and only one of its two M's goes. 'which is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to the elements, meaning the forces of nature such as wind and rain.

clue.text: Middle Eastern leader who planned raid on America

indicators.note: planned suggests the letters have been arranged into a scheme, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Middle Eastern ruler is accused of plotting an attack on the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'planned' rearranges RAID plus US. Darius the Great was a king of ancient Persia.
explanation.definitionFit: Darius was a Persian king, a ruler from the region now called the Middle East.

clue.text: Being at school and turning up to plunder

indicators.note: turning means the word up is flipped round to read the other way

parts.note: to plunder is to pillage

explanation.surface: A schoolboy is accused of looting on his way home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' flips UP to give PU.
explanation.definitionFit: Pupillage is the condition of being a pupil, so being at school fits as a noun phrase.

clue.text: Dance with hat out west, nothing more

indicators.note: out says the compass letter is taken away from the hat

parts.note: a bowler is a hard felt hat
W is the compass abbreviation for west
O, the round figure zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: A cowboy-hatted dancer in the Wild West, with nothing else on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes W (west) from BOWLER, leaving BOLER, and 'more' adds O. 'west' suggests the American West but just gives the letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The bolero is a lively Spanish dance in triple time.

clue.text: Politician's loud noise for 6

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', so the definition reads 'Politician is'

indicators.note: 6-down is LISTENER, so this says how the word strikes someone hearing it

parts.note: a loud harsh noise is a blare

explanation.surface: A loud noise made by a politician, as heard by an audience.
explanation.walkthrough: Tony Blair was the UK Prime Minister when this puzzle appeared.
explanation.definitionFit: Named British politician, Labour Prime Minister from 1997 to 2007.

clue.text: Set off on board ship for an audience

indicators.note: on board means carried within the ship

parts.note: a liner is a large passenger ship

indicators.note: off suggests something gone wrong, so the letters of the word Set are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone sets off on a cruise to hear a performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges SET to STE, which goes 'on board' LINER: LI-STE-NER.
explanation.definitionFit: A listener is a member of an audience, someone who hears a broadcast or performance.

clue.text: Performing star to 6

parts.note: 6-down is LISTENER: to a listener 'star' is heard as the surname Starr, and the clue wants the first name of the performer who used it

explanation.surface: A celebrity seen through the ears of an audience.
explanation.walkthrough: Ringo Starr was the Beatles' drummer; 'star' heard by a listener becomes his surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Stage first name of the Beatles drummer whose adopted surname sounds like 'star'.

clue.text: Solve mystery about kingcup

indicators.note: about means one piece is placed round another, here the cup round the king

parts.note: taken as written
Lear is the king of Shakespeare's tragedy

explanation.surface: A botanist tries to identify a puzzling marsh flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kingcup' is a real marsh flower (marsh marigold), which hides that the word splits in two, with the cup going 'about' the king.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to clear up a mystery is to explain or solve it.

clue.text: Shrub for odd 12 in dirty British boat

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: from Masefield's poem Cargoes, 'Dirty British coaster with a salt-caked smoke stack'

indicators.note: odd says the letters are made strange, so they are rearranged

parts.note: 12-across is NOTE

explanation.surface: A gardener loads a plant onto a grimy cargo vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dirty British coaster' is a famous line from John Masefield's poem Cargoes. 'odd' rearranges the 12-across answer, and 'in' puts the result inside the boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Cotoneaster is an ornamental shrub often grown for its red berries.

clue.text: Increased circulation without editor, which could be fatal

indicators.note: circulation suggests letters moving round, so the word is rearranged

explanation.surface: A newspaper's growing readership, minus its editor, could be deadly.
explanation.walkthrough: Take ED away ('without editor') from INCREASED and rearrange the rest ('circulation'). 'circulation' looks like newspaper sales.
explanation.definitionFit: Arsenic is a notorious poison, something that could kill.

clue.text: Provide for support with grub

parts.note: to provide food for people is to cater
a pillar is a support

explanation.surface: Someone offers to supply a meal and a prop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grub' looks like food after 'Provide for', but it is the insect larva.
explanation.definitionFit: A caterpillar is the grub, or larva, of a butterfly or moth.

clue.text: Government-sponsored revival of seaside peepshow?

parts.note: the old seaside slot machine was 'What the Butler Saw'; an official inquiry reporting again on what that servant saw would be his re-port

explanation.surface: Ministers pay to bring back the old pier-end slot machines.
explanation.walkthrough: The Butler Report (2004) was the UK government's inquiry into Iraq intelligence. 'What the Butler Saw' machines showed saucy flicker pictures on British piers.
explanation.definitionFit: Title of an official UK inquiry, chaired by Lord Butler, into pre-war intelligence.

clue.text: Fame acquired on the pitch

definitions.meaning: a musical sound at a set pitch

explanation.surface: A footballer becomes famous out on the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pitch' suggests a sports field but means musical pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: distinction or renown, and a musical tone of definite pitch.

clue.text: 12 has 1 in 4 in dread of a disastrous misjudgment

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held: '12 has 1 in 4 in dread of a disastrous misjudgment'. FA (a note, 12) + T(AL)ERROR is plain, but nothing sound makes '1 in 4' give AL: 1-across is MENDIP, 4-down PUPILLAGE; no blog found.
annotationWithheld.clue: 12 has 1 in 4 in dread of a disastrous misjudgment

clue.text: Restraint to turbulent stream in Holland

indicators.note: turbulent water is churned up, so the letters of stream are mixed

parts.note: a dam is a barrier restraining water

explanation.surface: A barrier is built against a rushing Dutch river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turbulent' rearranges the river word, and 'to' joins the restraint on after it. The definition 'in Holland' points to a place found there.
explanation.definitionFit: Amsterdam is the capital city located in the province of Holland, Netherlands.

clue.text: Leftover that's left over after marine exercise

indicators.note: after places that piece behind the rearranged word
exercise puts the word marine through its paces, rearranging it
over turns the word for left the other way round

parts.note: red describes the political left

explanation.surface: Whatever is still around once the Marines finish their drill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exercise' rearranges the soldier word; 'over' turns the left-wing colour backwards, and 'after' sets it at the end. 'Leftover' and 'left over' make a neat echo.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the remainder is whatever is left over after the rest is taken.

clue.text: Intensive poultry farm for veggies?

parts.note: an egg factory would be an ..., which vegetarians might think of as their kind of farm; really it is a vegetable

explanation.surface: A battery hen farm catering to vegetarians.
explanation.walkthrough: Eggplant is the American name for the aubergine.
explanation.definitionFit: Read whole, the clue suggests a factory producing eggs; the real thing is the purple vegetable.

clue.text: Alex's 21 perhaps helps to get a silent revolver

definitions.text: helps to get a silent revolver

indicators.note: perhaps marks the letters as just one possible version, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, including the S
21-down is EAGER

explanation.surface: A keen friend called Alex helps someone acquire a quiet handgun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges ALEXS with EAGER (21-down). The 'revolver' is not a gun but a turning wheel or axle.
explanation.definitionFit: Axle grease lubricates turning parts so a rotating wheel runs without squeaking.

clue.text: Member in team of African fighters

indicators.note: in places the member inside the team

parts.note: a team of eleven, written 11, read as two letter I's
MP, Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: One player in a squad of African soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: A team (football or cricket) has eleven players: '11' is taken as II.
explanation.definitionFit: An impi was a Zulu regiment, a body of southern African warriors.

clue.text: She's a good woman, if overfree

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', so the definition reads 'She is'

indicators.note: over places the first pieces above the last one in this down entry

parts.note: a saint, ST, is a supremely good person
to rid is to free

explanation.surface: A woman described as virtuous, though perhaps too generous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overfree' looks like one adjective but splits into 'over' (above, in a down clue) and 'free' (RID).
explanation.definitionFit: Astrid is a woman's first name, so it can stand for 'she'.

clue.text: Piglet's place at short notice

parts.note: in Winnie-the-Pooh, Piglet's house has a broken sign, a cut-short notice once warning off intruders

explanation.surface: A small pig is given somewhere to stay at very little warning.
explanation.walkthrough: Piglet claims the sign 'TRESPASSERS W' was his grandfather's name; it was the stump of 'Trespassers will be prosecuted'.
explanation.definitionFit: The words on the broken sign by Piglet's house are a shortened warning notice.

clue.text: Keen on Caribbean rock but rising with lack of gravity

indicators.note: with lack of says a letter is removed
rising means reading upwards in this down entry, so the word goes backwards

parts.note: reggae is Jamaican popular music
G is the physics symbol for gravity

explanation.surface: Keen on Jamaican music, yet floating up as if weightless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns REGGAE to EAGGER, and 'with lack of' removes one G (gravity). 'rock' looks like stone but means music.
explanation.definitionFit: Eager means keen, enthusiastically wanting to do something.

clue.text: Shoddy isn't a material

indicators.note: shoddy means badly made, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A remark that some poor goods aren't proper cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shoddy' rearranges ISNTA. Shoddy is also a cheap recycled-wool cloth, which helps the textile surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Satin is a smooth glossy fabric.

clue.text: Granny enlisted in military unit, like the Queen

indicators.note: enlisted in places grandma inside the regiment

parts.note: REGT abbreviates regiment
nan is a familiar word for a grandmother

explanation.surface: An elderly woman joins the army, behaving royally.
explanation.definitionFit: Regnant means reigning, as a queen regnant rules in her own right.

clue.text: Mocker of one featured in foreign articles

indicators.note: featured in places the number inside the pair of articles

parts.note: der is a German definite article
a second German der
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A satirist appears in some overseas newspaper pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'articles' looks like newspaper pieces but means grammatical words: two German DERs around I.
explanation.definitionFit: One who derides, ridicules or scoffs is a mocker.

clue.text: UK citizen possibly born outside it

indicators.note: outside puts the rearranged letters round the other word
possibly offers one arrangement of the word born, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A British national might be born abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges BORN to BRON, which goes 'outside' IT: BR-IT-ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A Briton is a native or citizen of Great Britain.

clue.text: Sailors' style before and in the present

indicators.note: before places the style ahead of the sailors

parts.note: a mode is a style or fashion
RN, the Royal Navy, stands for sailors

explanation.surface: A naval way of dressing, both old and up to date.
explanation.definitionFit: Modern means current, of the present time rather than the past.
